DBA is designed to be robust against rank instability and correlated errors, potentially outperforming simple mean/median by leveraging the geometric structure of the forecast space.

The current leader (DBA on pool4) performs well due to its robustness against the unstable ranking (tau=-0.201). To test if a more adaptive weighting scheme can outperform this robust average, I will try weighted combination using 'error_trend' weights which account for recent model performance changes, applied to the full pool to capture diverse signals.

The series has high trend strength and unstable ranking (ranking_tau=-0.201). DBA on a large pool (pool4) is currently leading, but its margin over median is narrow. I will test a simple mean on the top 8 models from the error table, which includes the most robust performers (NaiveMovingAverage, ETS, THETA, ARIMA, ONLY_CWT_catboost, ONLY_FT_rf, FT_catboost, NaiveSeasonal) to see if averaging their diverse strengths outperforms DBA's more complex aggregation.
